expectedText:
AGE AND ANTI-SOLICITATION EMPLOYMENT RESTRICTIONS FOR ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGE LICENSEES — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Acme Restaurant Group, Inc.

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California law restricting whom Acme Restaurant Group, Inc. may employ to sell, prepare, or serve alcoholic beverages, and certain employment arrangements the law prohibits on premises where alcoholic beverages are sold, under Business and Professions Code sections 25657 and 25663 (part of the Alcoholic Beverage Control Act, in the article of that Act captioned "Women and Minors"). It states facts about what those sections require, permit, and prohibit for a position such as Server held or sought by Jordan T. Reyes. It is not itself a hiring decision, a license determination, or advice about whether any specific job duties or employment arrangement complies with these sections. This document is distinct from this corpus's existing Minor Work Permits information sheet, which addresses the Education Code's school-issued work-permit system for minors under 18 generally, and from its Pre-Employment and Workplace Drug Testing and Physical Ability / Agility Pre-Employment Testing information sheets, which address different statutory and constitutional frameworks; this document instead addresses age- and conduct-based employment restrictions that apply specifically to licensees under the Alcoholic Beverage Control Act.

ON-SALE LICENSEES: PROHIBITION ON EMPLOYING ANYONE UNDER 21 TO PREPARE OR SERVE ALCOHOL
Business and Professions Code section 25663(a) prohibits a licensee that sells or serves alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises from employing any person under 21 years of age for the purpose of preparing or serving alcoholic beverages, subject to a separate statutory exception described elsewhere in this document. The same subdivision makes it a misdemeanor for any person to employ or use the services of someone under 21 in or on the portion of a premises, during business hours, that is primarily designed and used for the sale and service of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Except as provided in subdivision (c), no licensee that sells or serves alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises shall employ any person under 21 years of age for the purpose of preparing or serving alcoholic beverages. Every person who employs or uses the services of any person under the age of 21 years in or on that portion of any premises, during business hours, which are primarily designed and used for the sale and service of alcoholic beverages for consumption on the premises is guilty of a misdemeanor."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 25663(a) (California Legislative Information text), Business and Professions Code, on-sale prohibition on employing anyone under 21 to prepare or serve alcohol (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=25663.)
  Known gap: This clause states subdivision (a) of section 25663 as written. It does not address the age-18 rule for off-sale licensees or the 18-to-21 public-eating-place exception, each of which is described in a separate clause of this document.

OFF-SALE LICENSEES: RESTRICTION ON EMPLOYING ANYONE UNDER 18 TO SELL ALCOHOL
Business and Professions Code section 25663(b) states a separate rule for off-sale licensees: an off-sale licensee that employs or uses the services of a person under 18 years of age for the sale of alcoholic beverages is subject to suspension or revocation of its license, unless that person under 18 is under the continuous supervision of a person 21 years of age or older, in which case employment for that purpose is permitted.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Any off-sale licensee who employs or uses the services of any person under the age of 18 years for the sale of alcoholic beverages shall be subject to suspension or revocation of his or her license, except that a person under the age of 18 years may be employed or used for those purposes if that person is under the continuous supervision of a person 21 years of age or older."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 25663(b) (California Legislative Information text), Business and Professions Code, off-sale restriction on employing anyone under 18 to sell alcohol, and continuous-supervision exception (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=25663.)
  Known gap: This clause states subdivision (b) of section 25663 as written. It does not itemize the license suspension or revocation procedure that the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control applies when this subdivision is violated; that procedure is not addressed in this document.

EXCEPTION: EMPLOYEES 18 TO 21 SERVING ALCOHOL INCIDENTAL TO MEAL SERVICE IN A BONA FIDE PUBLIC EATING PLACE
Business and Professions Code section 25663(c) states the exception referenced in subdivision (a): a person between 18 and 21 years of age who is employed in a bona fide public eating place that is licensed for the on-sale of alcoholic beverages may serve alcoholic beverages to consumers, but only if the service occurs in an area primarily designed and used for the sale and service of food for consumption on the premises, and only if the employee's primary duties are the service of meals to guests, with alcohol service being incidental to those duties. For purposes of this subdivision, the statute defines "serve" or "service" to include the delivery, presentation, opening, or pouring of an alcoholic beverage.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "Any person between 18 and 21 years of age employed in any bona fide public eating place, as defined in Sections 23038 and 23038.1, which is licensed for the on-sale of alcoholic beverages, may serve alcoholic beverages to consumers only under the following circumstances: such service occurs in an area primarily designed and used for the sale and service of food for consumption on the premises; and the primary duties of the employee shall be the service of meals to guests, with the service of alcoholic beverages being incidental to such duties. For purposes of this subdivision, “serve” or “service” includes the delivery, presentation, opening, or pouring of an alcoholic beverage."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 25663(c) (California Legislative Information text), Business and Professions Code, exception permitting 18-to-21-year-old employees to serve alcohol incidental to meal service in a bona fide public eating place (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=25663.)
  Known gap: This clause states subdivision (c) of section 25663 as written. It does not itself determine, for any specific employee or work area, whether alcohol service is "incidental" to meal-service duties or whether an area is "primarily designed and used" for food service — factual questions the statute leaves to be assessed against its own text on particular facts. The statutory definition of "bona fide public eating place" that this subdivision cross-references is stated in a separate clause of this document.

STATUTORY DEFINITION: "BONA FIDE PUBLIC EATING PLACE"
Business and Professions Code section 23038 defines "bona fide public eating place," the term the section 25663(c) exception depends on, as a place regularly and in a bona fide manner used and kept open for the serving of meals to guests for compensation, with suitable kitchen facilities containing conveniences for cooking an assortment of foods required for ordinary meals, kept in a sanitary condition with proper refrigeration and in compliance with local health-department regulations. Section 23038.1 separately extends the same defined term, for the same statutory purposes, to certain publicly owned or leased convention centers, exhibit halls, or auditoriums that regularly serve meals to groups of guests under conditions that section states.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "“Bona fide public eating place” means a place which is regularly and in a bona fide manner used and kept open for the serving of meals to guests for compensation and which has suitable kitchen facilities connected therewith, containing conveniences for cooking an assortment of foods which may be required for ordinary meals, the kitchen of which must be kept in a sanitary condition with the proper amount of refrigeration for keeping of food on said premises and must comply with all the regulations of the local department of health."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 23038 (California Legislative Information text), Business and Professions Code, definition of "bona fide public eating place" (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=23038.)
  "Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 23038, “bona fide public eating place” also means a convention center, exhibit hall, or auditorium"
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 23038.1 (California Legislative Information text), Business and Professions Code, alternate definition of "bona fide public eating place" for certain convention centers, exhibit halls, and auditoriums (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=23038.1.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes only section 23038's core definitional sentence; it does not quote that section's further sentences defining "meals" and "guests" for purposes of the same section, or section 23038.1's fuller definition beyond the quoted opening clause identifying the convention-center category it adds. Whether a specific establishment meets either statutory definition is not determined by this document.

PROHIBITION ON EMPLOYING SOMEONE TO PROCURE OR ENCOURAGE ALCOHOL SALES FOR COMMISSION
Business and Professions Code section 25657(a) makes it unlawful for any person to employ, upon any licensed on-sale premises, another person for the purpose of procuring or encouraging the purchase or sale of alcoholic beverages, or to pay that person a percentage or commission on the sale of alcoholic beverages for procuring or encouraging such purchases or sales on the premises.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "For any person to employ, upon any licensed on-sale premises, any person for the purpose of procuring or encouraging the purchase or sale of alcoholic beverages, or to pay any such person a percentage or commission on the sale of alcoholic beverages for procuring or encouraging the purchase or sale of alcoholic beverages on such premises."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 25657(a) (California Legislative Information text), Business and Professions Code, prohibition on employment or commission arrangements to procure or encourage alcohol sales (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=25657.)
  Known gap: This clause states subdivision (a) of section 25657 as written. It does not address how this prohibition interacts with commission-based compensation for other, non-alcohol sales duties on the same premises; the statute's text addresses only commissions tied to procuring or encouraging alcoholic-beverage purchases or sales.

PROHIBITION ON EMPLOYING OR PERMITTING LOITERING TO SOLICIT ALCOHOL PURCHASES
Business and Professions Code section 25657(b) also makes it unlawful, in any place of business where alcoholic beverages are sold for consumption on the premises, to employ or knowingly permit anyone to loiter in or about the premises for the purpose of begging or soliciting a patron, customer, or visitor to purchase alcoholic beverages for the person doing the begging or soliciting. The same section states that every person who violates its provisions, including this prohibition and the commission-solicitation prohibition described in a separate clause of this document, is guilty of a misdemeanor.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-09]
  "In any place of business where alcoholic beverages are sold to be consumed upon the premises, to employ or knowingly permit anyone to loiter in or about said premises for the purpose of begging or soliciting any patron or customer of, or visitor in, such premises to purchase any alcoholic beverages for the one begging or soliciting."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 25657(b) (California Legislative Information text), Business and Professions Code, prohibition on employing or knowingly permitting loitering to solicit alcohol purchases (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=25657.)
  "Every person who violates the provisions of this section is guilty of a misdemeanor."
  — Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 25657 (California Legislative Information text), Business and Professions Code, misdemeanor penalty for violating section 25657 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&sectionNum=25657.)
  Known gap: This clause states subdivision (b) of section 25657 and the section's closing misdemeanor-penalty sentence as written. It does not address enforcement history, prosecutorial practice, or how this prohibition has been applied to particular business models by the Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control or the courts, none of which is addressed in this document.
